candidates.title: Parks Canada set to slash warden detachments, officers across national parks
candidates.description: Detachments will be closing in British Columbia, Alberta, Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Yukon and Northwest Territories. The number of wardens impacted by the decision is unknown, but CBC News has learned at least a dozen positions will be cut.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Drug runner? Arms dealer? The Adeline-C made waves in Halifax and beyond
candidates.description: The Adeline-C arrived in Halifax on Oct. 31, 1981, filled with state-of-the-art equipment, but it was soon abandoned by its crew. It would be years before its role in a complex U.S. drug smuggling operation worth as much as $200 million US became fully known.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cocaine smuggler could avoid prison as judge fears incarceration would orphan 7-year-old son
candidates.description: A Toronto judge is weighing whether to send a single father to prison for importing cocaine into Newfoundland and Labrador during the pandemic, or find an alternate sentence that could "break the cycle" for his seven-year-old boy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Many P.E.I. municipalities are seeing uncontested elections this year. Why aren't more people running?
candidates.description: There are 400 positions up for grabs across 56 municipalities, but many of those positions have already been acclaimed. In a total of 27 municipalities, all positions have been acclaimed, according to P.E.I.'s unofficial election results.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 4 dead, 2 in life-threatening condition after car crash in Puslinch, Ont.
candidates.description: Four people are dead and two others suffered life-threatening injuries after a single-vehicle crash in Puslinch — a rural area southwest of Guelph — early Saturday, according to Ontario Provincial Police.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian Crime Stoppers Association advises chapters to accept tips by phone only
candidates.description: The Canadian Crime Stoppers Association is advising its local chapters to solely accept tips by telephone instead of online, it said in a statement to CBC News on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: From sidelines to centre ice, a new women’s hockey league faces off in Fredericton
candidates.description: A new women's hockey league in Fredericton has hit the ice for its first season. The Fredericton Senior Recreational Women’s Hockey League is for women aged 30 and up who want to get out and play without the stress of high-level competition.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Number of unqualified Nunavut teachers nearly doubled in 5 years
candidates.description: The number of teachers who have letters of authority in Nunavut classrooms has nearly doubled in 5 years, from around 50 to now over 90. Nunavut's education minister David Akeeagok says he's not concerned about the increase, but the teachers’ union warns of the growing reliance on unqualified teachers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How witchcraft lore encouraged kindness among neighbours in Newfoundland and Labrador
candidates.description: Isolated in small communities with limited resources, rural Newfoundlanders and Labradorians had to rely on each other to survive. Thinking someone could bewitch you if you mistreated them was a reason to help all your neighbours, even the ones you didn’t particularly like.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian philanthropist Salah Bachir remembered for gifts to health care, 2SLGBTQ+ causes, education
candidates.description: Salah Bachir's friends and family remembered the executive, philanthropist and party host at his funeral as someone who always found ways to contribute, whether it was hosting family festivities at his historic home in Paris, Ont., soliciting donations for the Toronto dialysis unit where he was a patient or throwing gala fund-raising events for charities he cherished.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Important chapter of Catholic abuse saga comes to close, as N.L. court ends restructuring proceedings
candidates.description: A five-year restructuring process has now come to a close, with the corporation controlling the Archdiocese of St. John's selling off 132 properties and raising more than $30 million to compensate victims of abuse.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: WATCH: PAL Airlines flight loses wheel after landing in Wabush, N.L.
candidates.description: In an incident captured on video, a piece of the landing gear on a PAL Airlines plane came off during landing on Friday in Wabush.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian Para cyclist Mel Pemble earns track worlds silver with time trial personal best
candidates.description: Four-time Para cycling world champion Mel Pemble collected her second straight silver medal in the women’s C3 kilometre time trial at this year’s track competition in Apeldoorn, Netherlands on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal police chief defends push to change force's culture, weed out bad apples
candidates.description: As accusations of misconduct against Montreal’s police service mount, Chief Fady Dagher says he is taking concrete steps to bring change from the ground up while investigating and potentially prosecuting those "one per cent" of officers who "tarnish the uniform."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Body parts found in storage containers, documents show as Calgary couple appears in court
candidates.description: A Calgary couple facing a charge of committing indignity to a body is accused of placing human remains in storage containers, according to court records, and there are serious concerns about the husband’s mental health.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Feds tap Delta, B.C., port expansion as 'project of national interest'
candidates.description: The federal government has listed Roberts Bank Terminal 2 in Delta, B.C., as a "project of national interest" to expand and diversify Canada's trade capacity.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Victim of violent home invasion in Toronto's Bridle Path neighbourhood says family is 'traumatized'
candidates.description: The head of a Toronto real estate group says his family is traumatized and recovering after they were attacked in a violent home invasion in the Bridle Path neighbourhood Thursday morning.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'The woman from the hole': Winnipegger's comical quandary becomes Halloween costume
candidates.description: Christine Keilback might have the greatest sense of humour ever. She laughed off her misfortune after plunging shoulder-deep into a hole in a boulevard, and now she's getting a howl out of a Halloween costume inspired by it all.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New trial ordered for driver acquitted in crash that killed Vancouver toddler
candidates.description: Canada's top court has ordered a new trial for a man acquitted of dangerous driving charges in a crash that killed a B.C. toddler in 2021.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Civilians evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrive in Ukraine-held territory
candidates.description: Residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have crossed into Ukrainian-held territory after a humanitarian mission and localized ceasefire, part of a major rescue operation carried out under the most significant truce since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: This Texas midterm race has huge stakes, both for Donald Trump and the country
candidates.description: There's no U.S. midterm election with more at stake than the battle between Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico to become the next senator for Texas. The outcome could determine which party holds a majority in the U.S. Senate for the remainder of Donald Trump’s presidency.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'No one is safe' as Ebola outbreak surges to more than 10,000 cases, Africa's top doctor warns Canada
candidates.description: Africa's top doctor, who has called Canada home since 2013, tells CBC News there could be "massive" cross-border spread of Ebola in the months ahead as he calls for more international support.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Youth-led protests sweep across France, Europe for a 3rd weekend
candidates.description: Hundreds of thousands of mostly young protesters took to the streets across France on Saturday in a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over living costs and education. Youth-led demonstrations were also reported in Germany and Italy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Decision clearing path for Russia to join world juniors in Alberta is 'very unwelcome,' minister says
candidates.description: Canada's foreign affairs minister says the decision to let Russia back into the ice hockey world championships came as a "great disappointment" on Friday, as the country's ongoing invasion of Ukraine stretches toward its fifth year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Did human error cause Spain's deadly high-speed train crash? | About That
candidates.description: A high-speed train travelling at more than 150 km/h collided with a stopped train in central Spain, killing at least 69 people and injuring dozens more. Andrew Chang breaks down dispatcher audio and information about the railway's signalling system to explain how a technical glitch may have led to the fatal crash. (Photo credits: The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images)
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. charges 5 more Canadians with voter fraud offences amid Trump administration crackdown
candidates.description: The U.S. Department of Justice says charges have been laid against five more Canadians for voting fraud-related offences, the latest in a flurry of similar prosecutions ahead of next week's midterm elections.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: North American stocks sink, Wall Street suffers worst day since June amid tech sell-off
candidates.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite shed just under three per cent on Friday, while Canada's main index, the S&P/TSX composite index, finished the day down 1.7 per cent. Worries are rising about whether the hundreds of billions of dollars invested in AI will produce enough profit and productivity to make the investment worth it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pope Leo votes in U.S. midterms, Vatican confirms
candidates.description: The Vatican confirmed Friday that Pope Leo XIV had submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, citing his long-standing belief in civic participation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Binance says $6.3B US hacked in what could be largest cryptocurrency theft ever
candidates.description: A U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm says a North Korean unit was likely behind the hack that impacted more than $6 billion US on Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Aid operation, evacuations underway in Ukraine's stricken city of Oleshky
candidates.description: Starving and exhausted residents of a Russian-held town in southern Ukraine were being evacuated on Friday as part of a joint relief operation by the opposing sides, the first of its kind in four years and eight months of war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why the war in Iran might cost Trump and the Republicans at the ballot box
candidates.description: When Americans head to the ballot box, it is usually domestic issues that are at the front of mind, not foreign policy. But this time, Americans are linking the high price of gas and diesel with the U.S. war in the Middle East.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russia is back in the hockey world championships after sports court ruling
candidates.description: Russia teams must be allowed to play International Ice Hockey Federation events such as the world championships, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Australian court says mushroom poison murderer should never be released from prison
candidates.description: An Australian appeals court on Friday ordered triple-murderer Erin Patterson to never be released from prison because of the "shocking criminality" involved in poisoning four of her estranged husband's relatives with death cap mushrooms.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian economy stalled in August, points to September decline: StatsCan
candidates.description: Statistics Canada GDP data for August shows economic growth was essentially flat in August despite a rebound in retail trade that more than offset a decline in July. Wholesale trade, meanwhile, fell 1.4 per cent in August, as most subsectors contracted.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
candidates.description: Oleshky residents had been without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Clashes erupt between police and protesters in Paris
candidates.description: Over 320,000 people protested around France in a third weekend of demonstrations against the rising cost of living and poor public services.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
candidates.description: Two analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprit.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Police deployed during stand-off over control of top Poland court
candidates.description: The escalation came after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
candidates.description: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confronted his Russian counterpart at the meeting and accused his government of killing innocent civilians in Ukraine.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: They strangled us, says founder of Russian newspaper shut under pressure from authorities
candidates.description: Novaya Gazeta has been one of the most high-profile independent news outlets in Russia over the last three decades.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The fight to save Canadian town threatened by Trump's tariffs
candidates.description: A century-old paper mill in Témiscaming, Quebec is indefinitely closed after the US imposed 50% tariffs on its products, putting hundreds out of work.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
candidates.description: The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pontiff to vote in a US election
candidates.description: The Chicago-born pontiff, who has a tense relationship with Trump, mailed in a ballot for the midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
candidates.description: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Emotional reunions with loved ones for Oleshky evacuees
candidates.description: The BBC's Dan Johnson travelled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Blood donors get a Halloween fright in Thailand
candidates.description: Thai Red Cross workers dressed up as part of a Halloween-themed blood drive in the country's capital Bangkok.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: CCTV and zip ties: How US mail-in votes are secured and counted
candidates.description: BBC Verify goes to an election centre to get a behind-the-scenes look at how mail-in ballots for the US midterm elections are processed.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: He questioned Thailand's monarchy dressed as Harry Potter. Now he's in jail for 34 years
candidates.description: Thailand has prosecuted 294 people since 2020 under its lèse majesté law, with sentences going up to 50 years.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Responsible or panicked? Meet the people around the world already preparing for crisis
candidates.description: Filter straws to a disposable toilet - people in the US, Japan, Sweden and Netherlands on what's in their emergency stashes.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'The necktie is dead': How US midterm candidates are dressing for votes
candidates.description: From Alaska to Texas, candidates with an eye on Congress are using their personal style to stand out.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Democrats have an identity crisis - it won't be an easy fix
candidates.description: Whatever the result of the midterm elections, the party is facing tough questions over what they stand for and who should represent them.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Google value plunges by $500bn as its own AI search hits ad sales
candidates.description: Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its AI own search summaries were affecting ad revenue.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Who could be behind the Binance hack and what we know so far
candidates.description: Binance has been hit by what could be the biggest crypto hack ever - here's what we know so far
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: From Bitcoin to Binance: Crypto terms and what they mean
candidates.description: The Binance hack has thrust cryptocurrencies back into headlines - but what are they and how do they work?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: UK could see 10 days without rain after 'wettest week in two years'
candidates.description: With high pressure developing across the UK, the start of November is looking very settled with no significant rain in the forecast.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Six dead after helicopter crashes in northern Indian state
candidates.description: The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: France seethes again as youth-led protests sweep Europe
candidates.description: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez warned of a "very high risk" of disorder, especially after dark on Halloween, as some 320,000 people nationwide took to the streets.

candidates.title: Key takeaways from this week's political meeting in Beijing
candidates.description: The Communist party central committee meeting was focused on discipline and fighting corruption. It comes ahead of next year when Xi is widely expected to try to secure a fourth term.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Drone photo award winners: Far-out landscapes. Ship recycling. Rugs, rugs rugs!
candidates.description: The Siena Drone Photo Awards for 2026 offer breathtaking bird's-eye views of our planet, revealing landscapes, livelihoods and human stories often invisible from the ground.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Alaska's Senate race faces claims of spoiler candidate. And, Hegseth ousts Army general
candidates.description: Alaska's governor ordered an investigation into claims that Dems recruited a spoiler candidate to confuse voters. And, Hegseth ousted an Army general as the U.S. prepares for potential attacks on Iran.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israel is in a political deadlock. What comes next?
candidates.description: Israel's consequential election has ended in a deadlock, with neither side able to claim a majority, What happens now?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What killed 500-plus penguins? How scientists solved the mystery
candidates.description: The penguins that perished lived on the Danger Islands in Antarctica. The prime suspect was avian flu. Researchers were surprised by what they found.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A simple explainer of the massive $6.3 billion crypto heist at Binance
candidates.description: Here are five things to know about the massive hack of the crypto exchange Binance — from how it happened to what it means for the sector.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Plans for a data center threaten scenic wilderness and dark skies in West Virginia
candidates.description: Residents are fighting back against plans for a project that would span thousands of acres near the Monongahela National Forest and popular outdoor recreation, ski areas and dark sky sites.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Oil company earnings skyrocket — again
candidates.description: Oil companies are reporting another quarter of sky-high profits as the war in Iran pushes up the price of oil — and prices at the pump.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Hackers steal over $6 billion from crypto exchange Binance in staggering heist
candidates.description: More than $6 billion worth of cryptocurrencies were stolen from Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange. It's the biggest cyber heist ever — and many suspect North Korea may be behind it.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Binance flags 'potential security issue,' says approximately $6.3 billion impacted
candidates.description: It wasn't immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered. The company said its teams are "working around the clock" to resolve the issue.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The two most interesting risks to Anthropic
candidates.description: Anthropic gave a 94-page list of risk factors in its S-1 this week. Two of them stood out.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Candy prices got you scared stiff? What to know about the cost of Halloween this year
candidates.description: Prices for candy, the most popular Halloween purchase, and gum have risen 7.7% in one year and are up more than 18% in two years, according to the latest federal data.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'Affordability? For who?' Voters decide between helping homeowners or public services
candidates.description: Candidates across the U.S. have paid lip service to affordability issues. In Florida, the question of how to save voters money, and at what cost, is literally on the ballot.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How powerful is Elon Musk? How his political influence compares to past U.S. moguls
candidates.description: Critics say the tech entrepreneur's enormous wealth has given him too much political power. But when stacked up against other notable American moguls, historians say he's not unique.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Do you have seasonal affective disorder? How to tell — and what to do about it
candidates.description: The syndrome can make people feel like a "hibernating bear," says Dr. Norman Rosenthal, who published the first research on SAD. He explains how to identify the symptoms and what to do to feel better.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows
candidates.description: Most kids say they use chatbots for help with homework and when they're stressed, lonely, or anxious. And how they use chatbots is tied to their mental health.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Florida sees spike in dengue fever cases
candidates.description: Florida is seeing a record number of dengue fever cases this year as the tropical disease thrives in warming climates.

candidates.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur. * WHERE...A portion of south central Colorado, including the following areas, the Eastern San Juan Mountains, and the Upper Rio Grande Valley. * WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location. Rockslides will be possible in the mountainous areas. Highway 160 and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Heavy rainfall is expected to fall Sunday and Monday across the area, leading to elevated concerns for flooding in areas that have recently received excessive moisture, or have recently experienced flooding. - The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and the South Fork of the Rio Grande, including South Fork and Mogote. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
